# sv0c/sv0vm: floating-point + wide-int on the VM backend

## purpose

Close the C-backend / VM-backend disconnect that blocks **`sv0-mathlib`**
completion. `sv0-mathlib` is 100% "Tier 1" (pure sv0 arithmetic — `+ - * /`,
comparisons, bitwise; no libm, no special opcodes) and its spec
(`~/Documents/project-specs/sv0-mathlib/SPEC.md` §5.1, COMPAT-001, COMPAT-002,
TEST-005) makes **cross-backend parity a release gate**. Today the VM toolchain
path cannot compile or run floating-point code at all, and silently narrows
`i64`/`u64` to 32 bits, so none of those gates can be met.

This task takes **Option B** (chosen 2026-08-29): extend the **native VM
bytecode emitter** (`scripts/build-sv0-megatu-vm-native.sh` + `sv0c/lib/vm_codegen.sv0`)
rather than the frozen SML bootstrap path (`sv0c/sml-legacy/`). Rationale below.

Slices: **`VMF-001…021`** (this file is the hub *and* the slice backlog — small
enough not to need a separate checklist).

## why Option B, and why it is smaller than it looks

`./scripts/sv0 vm-compile` / `vm-project-compile` today shell into the **frozen
SML bootstrap compiler** (`Main.main [..., "--target=vm", ...]`). A float dies at
three of the four pipeline stages there:

| # | stage | file | float status |
|---|-------|------|--------------|
| 1 | AST→IR lowering | `sml-legacy/ir/lowering.sml:265` `lowerLit` | `FloatLit` → `raise Fail "literal not supported in lowering slice"` |
| 2 | IR→bytecode | `sml-legacy/backend/vm/vm_codegen.sml:137` | `I.VFloat _ => raise Fail "vm: float in bytecode slice"`; `binopToInsn` emits `ADD_I32` **unconditionally** (no i64 either) |
| 3 | `.sv0b` encode | `sv0vm/src/bytecode/bytecode.sml` (+ a copy in `sml-legacy/backend/vm/`) | **already float-ready** — `PUSH_F64` (op 6), `*_F64` (48–52), `f64Le` encoder, `PUSH_I64` (5), `*_I64` (32–37) all present |
| 4 | interpreter | `sv0vm/src/interpreter/interpreter.sml` | `cell = CInt \| CBool \| CUnit \| CStrIdx` — no float/i64 cell; dispatch is an "i32 slice", unknown opcodes hit `_ => raise Fail "opcode not implemented in this slice"` (line ~502) |

**Corrections that the deep read (2026-08-29) forced — these de-risk Option B:**

1. **The native VM emitter is not broken.** The alarming header in
   `build-sv0-megatu-vm-native.sh` ("panics … pending the IR-ADT bridge") is
   **stale**. Per `sv0c/doc/archive/l0-closure-roadmap.md` §D1b–D5, the native
   emitter was driven to **byte-identical parity with the SML `--target=vm`
   reference for all 17 mega-TU compiler modules** (sv0c `6040a7a`, 2026-08-05),
   made the **default** tier-2 emitter, and CI-gated
   (`.github/workflows/vm-parity-tier2.yml`). IR-ADT convergence, slot
   allocation, structs, enums, `match`, loops, `box_new` unpacking — all done and
   byte-clean. Option B = "extend a working, tested emitter across two type
   classes it has never seen" + the runtime side. **Fix that stale header as
   step 0.**

2. **The IR ADTs did quietly re-drift, but harmlessly.** `lib/lowering.sv0`'s
   shared `enum Value` has 10 variants: tags 0–7 shared, then `VFloat(i32)` = tag
   8 and `VIntWide(i32)` = tag 9, **appended** (comment: "keep this enum's layout
   a prefix-compatible match"). `lib/vm_codegen.sv0`'s `enum Value` still has only
   the 8 shared variants — bug #5 / bug #1 added float/wide to lowering for the C
   backend and never mirrored them. A `VFloat` box reaching `emit_value` falls
   through all 8 arms → `return -1` → `emit_program < 0` → compose-main **exit 5**
   (a clean, diagnosable failure — *not* a panic or miscompile). Re-adding tags
   8/9 restores the invariant.

3. **Project mode is a real but small gap.** `build-sv0-megatu-vm-native.sh`
   reads one path from `SV0_DRV_REQUEST`. The C native compiler gets `--project`
   from a Python-injected snippet in `build-sv0-megatu-native.sh` that calls
   `link_project_concat_sources_from_dir(dir)` — pure source-concat into one TU
   (that fn already lives in the mega-TU). The VM recipe needs the same branch.
   **Bonus:** this means `sv0-mathlib`'s `E0304: duplicate type Option` VM
   blocker (`BUGS.md` "Not yet working") **does not exist on the native VM path**
   — that bug is in SML's per-file linker; native `--project` is source-concat,
   one TU, one `Option`. Option B sidesteps it for free.

4. **There is no SML float/i64 reference to byte-diff against.**
   `sml-legacy/backend/vm/vm_codegen.sml` raises on `VFloat` and only ever emits
   `ADD_I32`. So the Phase-D "byte-identical vs `golden/sml/*.sv0b`" harness
   **cannot validate any float or wide-int program**, and enabling `ADD_I64` in
   the native emitter would make its output *diverge* from the frozen SML goldens
   for any i64 program. For the new surface, parity must be **behavioral**:
   native-`emit-c`→run vs native-VM-emit→`sv0vm`-run, compared bit-exact
   (int/modular) or ULP (float) — which is exactly what COMPAT-001/002 and SPEC
   §16.2 specify anyway. This is a **new harness**, not a reuse of tier-2
   byte-diff.

**Net:** Option B's genuine extra cost over Option A (extend `sml-legacy/`) is the
emitter work landing in `vm_codegen.sv0` instead of `vm_codegen.sml`, plus one
sub-decision (VMF-D). In exchange: work in the living codebase not the frozen
one, get project mode via source-concat, sidestep the `E0304` linker bug, and end
with the native emitter as the single source of truth. The interpreter work
(VMF-010…013) and the behavioral parity harness (VMF-018) are required by **any**
path that runs float on the VM — not Option-B-specific.

## spot-verification (2026-08-29) — "purely additive" assumption CONFIRMED

Grepped all 17 tier-2 modules (`span token ast bytecode env include_expand lexer
resolver parser main diagnostic ir types unify codegen checker lowering`) plus the
broader `manifest.txt` VM-parity-v1 set (integration + `vm_*.sv0` programs):

- **Zero** `i64`/`u64`/`f64`/`f32`/`u32` typed locals/params/returns outside
  comments. (3 hits — `bytecode.sv0:347`, `lowering.sv0:5115`, `checker.sv0:3761`
  — all in doc comments.)
- **Zero** float literals. (`lexer.sv0:881` `"3.14 rest"` is *inside a string
  literal*; the rest are comments citing sv0-mathlib.)
- **Zero** integer literals exceeding `i32` range in any gated program.
  `codegen.sv0` `2147483647` fits exactly; `vm_codegen_jump_patch_core.sv0`
  `2147483645/6` are `i32::MAX−2/−1`; `"-2147483648"` is a *string* literal.

**⇒ The 17 tier-2 byte-goldens will be completely unaffected by VMF-001…009.**
Every operand in those modules stays `category 0 = int`; every binop resolves to
the existing I32 opcodes. S1–S3 cannot regress tier-2 byte parity.

**New finding from the sweep — a constraint for the i64 track (VMF-008):**
`test/integration/int_min/int_min.sv0` (NOT in any VM-parity manifest, so not a
gate today) does `let a: i32 = 0 - 2147483648;` and its README asserts the
`2147483648` literal **wraps to INT_MIN on every backend** (BH-7). The C backend
gets this via C's implicit narrowing on `int a = 2147483648;`. The VM has no
implicit narrowing, so **`VIntWide` emission must respect the declared type
context** — truncate to i32 when the target is `i32`, only emit a real `PUSH_I64`
when the context is `i64`/`u64`. Add this as an explicit constraint + a
regression fixture (VMF-008 / VMF-017).

### Phase 2 — sv0vm interpreter wide cells (`sv0vm/src/interpreter/interpreter.sml`)

The `.sv0b` **decoder** (`sv0vm/src/bytecode/bytecode.sml`) already decodes
opcodes 5/6/32-37/48-52. Only interpreter dispatch is the "i32 slice"
(`_ => raise Fail "opcode not implemented in this slice"`).

- **VMF-010/011/012 · wip** (one commit — the datatype change forces all three):
  - `datatype cell` gains `CF64 of real` + `CI64 of Int64.int`; `truthy` cases.
  - `arithFF` (`Real.+/-/*/~`) + `arithLL` (`Word64` wrap for add/sub/mul,
    `Int64.quot/rem` for div/mod) + `w64`/`unw64`; dispatch `PUSH_F64`→CF64,
    `PUSH_I64`→CI64, `ADD_F64`(48)…`NEG_F64`(52), `ADD_I64`(32)…`NEG_I64`(37).
  - `cmp` refactored to a `{ii, rr, ll}` record so one polymorphic opcode
    dispatches int/i64/f64 by cell kind; `cmpEQ`…`cmpGTE` vals; real comparators
    are `Real.</==/…` (IEEE NaN⇒false, never `Real.compare` which raises).
  `make check` clean. `sv0vm/test/bytecode_test.sml` +14 rows (f64/i64
  arith+cmp via `sel`, incl. `i64-mul-wrap` 2^32·2^32→0 and wide values wrong
  under `CInt`). `integration-vm` all-pass.
  **End-to-end verified**: `f64run.sv0` (`1.5+2.5>3.9` → exit 7) and
  `i64run.sv0` (`5e9+3e9>7999999999` → exit 9) both emit via
  `build/sv0-megatu-vm-native` and **run correctly on sv0vm**, and the exit
  codes **match the native C backend** — first cross-backend f64/i64 parity.
  Full `./scripts/sv0 test` running.
- **VMF-013 · wip** — f64 through structs, `match`, contracts end to end.
  - Structs with `f64` fields + field access: emit + run OK (cells flow through
    `ALLOC_STRUCT`/`GET_FIELD` unchanged).
  - **VMF-013a — pre-existing native-VM-emitter contract bug FIXED.** The native
    emitter panicked (`vec: index out of bounds`) on **any** `requires`/`ensures`
    program (pure i32 too), because `vm_codegen.contract_pool_key` stores a
    negative sentinel `-(kind·1e6 + fn_h + 1)` in the string pool and
    `bytecode.sv0`'s `encode_strings` deref'd it as a token handle
    (`vec_get(starts, -43)`). Never caught: the 17 tier-2 modules have no
    contracts; `contracts.sv0` only ran the SML `--target=vm` path. Confirmed
    pre-existing at baseline `52d28ea`. Fix: `encode_strings` now detects
    `idx < 0` and calls new `decode_contract_key` → `"requires failed: <fn>"` /
    `"ensures failed: <fn>"` bytes (mirrors SML's
    `poolAdd ("requires failed: " ^ fnName)`). Result: `contracts.sv0` native
    emit is now **byte-identical to the SML golden** → added to
    `tier2-manifest.txt` (**18/18**). `f64struct.sv0` (`Pair2{hi:f64,lo:f64}` +
    `requires(p.hi>=0.0) ensures(result>=p.lo)`) emits + runs → `vm_exit:11`,
    matching the C backend. Contract *violation* fires: VM `sv0 contract
    violation: requires failed: need_pos` / exit 1, matching C's exit 1 (message
    text: VM uses the SML `": "` form, C uses `" in "` — cosmetic stderr diff,
    exit codes match).

### Phase 3 — project mode + native-VM-emitter language completeness

- **VMF-014 · done** (parent `5dcfce7`): `build-sv0-megatu-vm-native.sh`'s
  injected CLI-read handles `--project <dir>` (source-concat via
  `link_project_concat_sources_from_dir`, one TU). A 2-file f64 project
  (`scale` in `lib/` + `main.sv0`) VM-emits + runs = C exit 22. tier-2 18/18.
- **VMF-016 · done (implicit)**: one-TU source-concat means the SML `--project`
  path's per-file `E0304 duplicate type` cannot arise on the native VM path.
  The full `sv0-mathlib` project resolves + type-checks fine through the native
  VM pipeline (fails only later, at emit — see 014a).
- **VMF-014a · done — ALL of `sv0-mathlib` now VM-compiles AND runs, matching
  the C backend.** Three linked fixes (root-caused one at a time by re-emitting
  `--project sv0-mathlib` and following each failure):
  1. **`lowering.sv0` — struct-typed `result` slot.** `ensures(result.re == a &&
     result.im == b)` failed to VM-emit: `lower_fn` emitted `Instr::DeclVar(ret_slot)`
     (scalar, width 1, no field layout), which the C backend papers over via its
     tyenv but the VM emitter does not. Fix: emit `Instr::DeclNamed(ret_ty_tok,
     ret_slot)` when the fn's return type (via `lower_scan_fn_ret_ty_tok`) is not
     plain `i32`/`bool`/`unit` — more correct for the C side too (`double
     result;` not `int result;`). Not float-specific (i32 structs hit it too);
     the 17 tier-2 modules never put `result.field` in a compound contract.
  2. **`vm_codegen.sv0` — spilled-temp category (`two_prod`).** A spilled
     sub-expression temp (`Assign(t, <expr>)`) got category 0, so
     `(f64 + f64) + (f64 * f64)` over two such temps emitted `ADD_I32` →
     interpreter `arithmetic on non-int`. New `expr_cat` (mirrors
     `megatu_expr_category`) + `ensure_var_cat`; `scan_instr_env`'s `Assign`/
     `Store` now categorize the dest from the RHS expr.
  3. **`vm_codegen.sv0` + recipe — call-result category (`tan_f64`).**
     `sin_f64(x) / cos_f64(x)`: lowering always passes `Instr::Call.rty = 0`, so
     call-result temps were category 0. New `bretcats` (per-block return
     category, block-indexed) built in the VM compose main from `frt` +
     `megatu_cty_of_root`, threaded through `emit_fn`/`local_count_and_env`/

## VMF-D — sub-decision: f64 literal → IEEE-754 bits

`VFloat(h)` gives the emitter the literal's *token* (e.g. `"3.14"`); it must emit
the 8-byte double bit pattern. sv0-the-compiler has no float type, no float parse,
no float runtime builtin. Two options:

| | **D-int: pure-integer strtod-to-bits in sv0** | **D-builtin: one narrow runtime builtin** |
|---|---|---|
| mechanism | ~150–250 lines in `bytecode.sv0`: parse mantissa+exp, normalize, **round-half-to-even to 53 bits**, assemble sign/exp/frac | `sv0_f64_bits(s) -> (lo,hi)` in `sv0_runtime.c` = `strtod` + `memcpy`; wire through checker/resolver/lowering/`megatu_builtin_*`; emitter calls it |
| correctness risk | real — rounding-edge bugs → non-bit-identical `.sv0b` → surfaces as ULP/accuracy failures, hard to attribute | near-zero — delegates to libc `strtod` |
| language purity | keeps the toolchain 100% float-free (a stated project value) | adds a float-touching builtin — but **only reachable from the VM emitter**, never in emitted user code |
| effort | high, self-contained, table-testable | low, but touches 4 compiler subsystems + the builtin-id remap the roadmap already flags as "latently mis-indexed" |

**Recommendation: D-builtin**, isolated as `sv0_f64_bits` with an "emitter-only"
doc note; fall back to D-int only if float-free is non-negotiable.

**DECIDED (2026-08-29): D-int — pure-integer strtod-to-bits in sv0.** Keep the
toolchain 100% float-free. Implemented as its own bigint-backed
decimal→IEEE-754 routine in `vm_codegen.sv0` (or a sibling), **correctly
rounded** (round-half-to-even), validated against a checked-in hex table. Split
into 7b–7e (see the micro-slice list). Accepts the correctness risk; mitigated
by a broad literal→hex-pattern unit table covering exact values, `0.1`-class
rounding, subnormals, and overflow/underflow.
